q: How does a Chhattisgarh silico-manganese plant work out carbon per tonne?
title: Chhattisgarh SiMn: carbon per tonne
short: Add the CO2 from reductants by carbon mass balance to the CO2 from the electricity your furnaces use, then divide by tonnes of alloy. Silico-manganese is excluded from CBAM, so this is a footprint for buyers and lenders, not a CBAM figure.
audience: Silico-manganese and ferromanganese plants in Chhattisgarh, around Raipur and Bilaspur

p: Carbon in coke, coal and electrode paste, minus carbon leaving in the alloy, slag and dust, times 44/12. Tonnes of each reductant come from purchase and stock records, carbon content from the supplier analysis.
Furnace kWh from the meter times the grid factor, 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh from the CEA database, or your captive plant's own factor if you generate.

sections.h: Why it matters even without CBAM
p: Steelmakers abroad count your alloy in their own figures and ask for it. A clear per tonne number with its workings is easier to defend than a range from a trade body.

example.title: Illustrative footprint for one tonne of silico-manganese
lines: Coke: 420 kg x 85% carbon = 357 kg C; carbon in alloy 1.5% = 15 kg C
Total: about 4.1 t CO2 per tonne of alloy
example.note: Inputs are illustrative. Use your own furnace data, slag carbon and electricity meter readings.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
